headline: Congress made lynching a federal hate crime and set criminal penalties for conspiring to commit certain hate crimes.
what_it_does: The law makes lynching a federal hate crime offense. It sets penalties of a fine, a prison term of up to 30 years, or both, for a person who conspires to commit a hate crime that causes death or serious bodily injury, or that includes kidnapping, aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to kill.

who_it_affects.group: People who conspire to commit federal hate crimes
who_it_affects.how: They can face a fine, up to 30 years in prison, or both if the conspiracy involves a hate crime that results in death or serious injury or includes kidnapping, aggravated sexual abuse, or an attempt to kill.
They have a federal hate crime charge available for lynching and for qualifying hate-crime conspiracies.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed into law on March 29, 2022. The official summary does not list a separate later effective date.
